narrative: The model estimated a 41% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That is not a forecast that you will certainly default, but it was above the approval cutoff used by the bank, so your application was declined. The strongest reason was your checking-account position: a balance in the 0–200 DM range was the most influential factor increasing your assessed risk. The second most important factor was the amount you requested. At 4,297 DM it is above the average approved request of about 3,020 DM, but in your case this amount was the main element working in your favour and lowered the risk estimate. The third factor was your property position. Having no recorded property or unknown property details increased the risk assessment, and only about 7.8% of approved applicants had this profile. To improve your position, ask the bank which approval criteria you missed and whether a manual review is possible. Provide recent bank statements and evidence of any assets, savings or property, and ask how to strengthen your checking-account profile. You could also discuss adding a guarantor or co-applicant, and whether a different request structure would meet the bank’s criteria.
